$comment: The shared cross-family base schema. Hosting settled 2026-09-16: all four families' schemas are hosted under the Polymathie parent brand at Polymathie-Studio/tools/schema as GitHub raw URLs; each family's source registers, models, and generators stay in that family's own tools repo, and the generated schema is published across into this one host. Creating the Polymathie-Studio/tools repo and publishing this file there is the pending smaller reorganization; the $id is fixed now so families can reference it. A larger reorganization under a top-level Polymathie org is deferred by Durgadas, so this host is interim and the URLs migrate later. Generalized from the DS4AI Polymathie manifest schema (~/code/missing/manifest.schema.json) by lifting the family-agnostic core out and pushing domain-specific structure into the open 'domain' extension.
title: Standards family manifest (cross-family base)
description: The family-agnostic base descriptor for a standards family, shared across the Coordination Structural Integrity Suite, the CRAFT family, and the Polymathie DS4AI suite. A family's manifest validates against this base; family-specific structure lives in the open 'domain' extension so the core stays shared and each domain stays precise. The machine-readable layer is derived from canonical source by a generator, never hand-maintained.

suite.description: The AI-facing or product suite name, if distinct from the family or publisher (e.g. 'DS4AI, the Design Suite for AI').

publisher.description: The organization, studio, or author that publishes the family.

version.description: The manifest's own version (moves as the family releases).

canonicalSourceRepo.description: The repository holding the canonical source documents the machine layer is derived from.

generatedBy.description: The generator that emits this manifest from canonical source. Present because the layer is derived, never hand-maintained; running it is a publish gate.

surfaces.description: The distribution surfaces the family anticipates, each with a status and notes. Optional and shared.

members.description: The standards or instruments the family publishes.

conformance.description: Where the family's structured conformance report is emitted and the schema it validates against.

report.description: Path to the emitted structured conformance report.

schema.description: Path to the machine-readable schema of the family's checks.

agentInstruction.description: Pointer to the family's AGENTS.md (the skill layer between prose and machine-readable).

domain.description: The per-family domain extension: the structure specific to this family (e.g. DS4AI invisible-correctness axes, CSIS compressive/generative families and corollaries, CRAFT conditions). Shape is family-specific and deliberately not constrained by the base.

kind.description: The member's kind, e.g. standard, specification, instrument, primitive, standard-candidate.

status.description: Publication status. 'candidate' carries the not-promoted, not-a-conformance-gate meaning so a consumer never mistakes a candidate for a settled standard.

group.description: Optional within-family grouping, e.g. compressive, generative, or an axis name.

canonicalSource.description: Path or URL to the canonical source document. The machine layer points at this rather than reproducing prose (substrate discipline).

machineReadable.description: Pointers to this member's own machine-readable files (structured export, schema, runnable conformance entry point). Extensible.

packaging.description: Per-surface distribution slots. Extensible and heterogeneous; slot shape is not constrained.
